title: Finite-diagram and Hom descent from the object and arrow colimits
statement: Let J be a small filtered category and F : J → Cat. Let O be the chosen object-set colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], equipped with a category structure and functors V_j whose object maps are its coprojections and which commute with transitions. Suppose a colimit cocone of the arrow sets is equivalent to Arrow O, intertwining the coprojections with the arrow maps of V_j [def-weil-pbc-arrows-functor]. Then finite lists of objects and arrows lift with every source, target, identity and composition relation; two finite lists with equal images agree at a common refinement; every functor from a finite category lifts to a stage; and the stage Hom sets represent every Hom in O, with equality exactly at a common refinement whose maps out of the starting stage commute.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 09YL (lemma-colimit-sites), first paragraph: 'The formula C = colim C_i means that Ob(C) = colim Ob(C_i) and Arrows(C) = colim Arrows(C_i). Then source, target, and composition are inherited ... Remark that given any finite diagram in C there exists an i such that this diagram is the image of a diagram in C_i' (stated without proof); filtered colimits of sets: categories.tex Section Tag 04AX

proof.text: Obtain finite-list lifts from the finite-lifting lemma and eventual equality from the simultaneous-list equality lemma. Construct the lifted finite functor from these finite-list lifts using the finite-functor lifting theorem.

For Hom representability, lift the two endpoint objects and the given arrow using lists of lengths two and one. Compare the lifted endpoint list with the original stage endpoints via simultaneous list equality. Map the lifted arrow to this common stage and transport its endpoints to obtain a morphism between the transitioned original objects. Arrow.mk is unchanged by endpoint transports. Compatibility of V gives the required image equality.

For equality of Hom representatives, apply simultaneous list equality to an empty object list and a singleton arrow list. Equalize the two maps out of the starting stage using IsFiltered.coeqHom, then map the equality of arrows along that equalizer. Functor.map_comp gives the required stage equality. Conversely map a given refinement equality by V and use functor compatibility on both sides.

proof_origin.place: Tag 09YL, first paragraph and Hom calculation, using Categories Tag 04AX; finite list and finite functor components separated, Hom argument proved explicitly in Lean
